text:
Cutter Gauthier has scored in seven straight games, 14 goals in all, a run headlines put beside Mario Lemieux and Alexander Mogilny. He has points in nine straight, and our numbers say the chances are real, not just the finish. Tonight we have him at 48% to score, the highest of anyone in this game. The Ducks' five-game winning streak ended Wednesday against Nashville, but they sit at 21 points with a 61% playoff chance in our simulations.

The Islanders bring a teenage headliner of their own. Matthew Schaefer scored a power-play goal in his 100th game on Thursday and has 11 points in his last ten. He is one of our sleepers: 72% for a point tonight, well above his season pace of 57%, because the Ducks give up the sixth-most expected goals per 60. Bo Horvat plays his 900th NHL game, and that 5-2 win in Los Angeles snapped a four-game winless run.

Our other sleeper is Victor Eklund, who has goals in four straight on a third line beside Brayden Schenn, taking Calum Ritchie's spot. Asked what's working, he said "I have no idea," as Stefen Rosner of NHL.com posted it. The numbers have an idea: 3.2 expected goals in his last ten games, better than 93% of depth forwards. We have him at 22% to score and 39% for a point. Sleepers are for information only.

Neither starter is confirmed yet. Semyon Varlamov is expected for New York over Ilya Sorokin, five goals better than expected in five games, and Lukas Dostal is expected for Anaheim at .866. Watch the penalty box: the Ducks take 5.1 penalties a game and the Islanders' penalty kill allows 0.90 expected goals a game, the most of either unit here. Travis Mitchell faces the club he played nine games for, and New York won the first meeting 3-2 in October.
headline: Gauthier's goal streak meets Schaefer's Islanders
